definition.def: If you distort a statement, fact, or idea, you report or represent it in an untrue way.
examples: The media distorts reality; categorises people as all good or all bad. [VERB noun]
The minister has said his remarks at the weekend have been distorted. [VERB noun]

definition.def: If something you can see or hear is distorted or distorts, its appearance or sound is changed so that it seems unclear.
examples: A painter may exaggerate or distort shapes and forms. [VERB noun]
His size was persistently distorted by the cartoonists. [VERB noun]
This caused the sound to distort. [VERB]

definition.def: pulled out of shape so that it looks strange; made to sound strange
examples: The song features lots of crazy distorted guitar.

definition.def: presented in a way that changes them so that they are no longer correct or true
examples: The article gave a distorted picture of his childhood.
He presents a grossly distorted view of the issues.

examples.sentence: As Peter Derks, a psychologist at William and Mary College in Virginia, says: "I like to think of humour as the distorted mirror of the mind.
Some have even conducted staged representations of the painting in order to ascertain whether Manet's seemingly distorted point of view might have been possible after all.
